The '''35th Academy Awards''', honoring the [[1962 in film|best in film for 1962]], were held on April 8, 1963, at the [[Santa Monica Civic Auditorium]] in [[Santa Monica, California]], hosted by [[Frank Sinatra]].

The year's most successful film was [[David Lean]]'s ''[[Lawrence of Arabia (film)|Lawrence of Arabia]]'', with 10 nominations and 7 wins, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and Lean's second win for [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]]. For his role as [[T. E. Lawrence]], [[Peter O'Toole]] received his first of eight career nominations for [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]], all unsuccessful; as of the [[94th Academy Awards]], O'Toole and [[Glenn Close]] share the record for the most acting nominations with no wins. 

[[Arthur Penn]]'s ''[[The Miracle Worker (1962 film)|The Miracle Worker]]'' earned the rare distinction of winning two acting Oscars ([[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for [[Anne Bancroft]] and [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] for [[Patty Duke]]) ''without'' a nomination for Best Picture. The only other film to do this to date was ''[[Hud (1963 film)|Hud]]'', the [[36th Academy Awards|following year]].

==Ceremony==
The [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] Oscar occasioned the last act of the long-running feud between [[Joan Crawford]] and [[Bette Davis]]. They had starred together for the first time in ''[[What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? (film)|What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?]]'', a surprise hit the previous summer. Davis was nominated for her role as the title character, a faded child star who humiliates the wheelchair-using sister who eclipsed her fame in adulthood, while Crawford was not.<ref name="Slate piece">{{cite news|last=Longworth |first=Karina |title=Did Bette and Joan Really Have a ''Feud''? |url=http://www.slate.com/articles/arts/you_must_remember_this/2017/03/did_bette_and_joan_really_feud_or_was_it_a_publicity_stunt.html |newspaper=[[Slate (website)|Slate]] |date=March 10, 2017 |access-date=April 27, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170401051200/http://www.slate.com/articles/arts/you_must_remember_this/2017/03/did_bette_and_joan_really_feud_or_was_it_a_publicity_stunt.html |archive-date=April 1, 2017 }}</ref>

Crawford told the other nominated actresses that, as a courtesy, she would accept their awards for them should they be unavailable on the night of the ceremony. Davis did not object as her rival had often done this, but, on the night of the ceremony, she was livid when Crawford took the stage, wearing what was described as a "radiant smile",<ref name="Oscars '62 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/842/mode/2up |title=The People's Almanac |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |isbn=0-385-04060-1 |location=Garden City, New York |page=842}}</ref> to cheerfully accept the award on behalf of [[Anne Bancroft]], who had a [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] commitment. Davis believed that Crawford had told other Oscar voters to vote for ''[[The Miracle Worker (1962 film)|The Miracle Worker]]'' star in order to upstage her. The rekindled animosity between the two resulted in Crawford leaving the cast of ''[[Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte]]'', a planned follow-up to ''Baby Jane'' that began filming the next summer, early in production.<ref name="Slate piece" />
